Stops bleeding: clotting and vessel constriction slow blood loss from wounds and internal bleeds.
Repairs soft tissue: bruises, cuts and torn muscle knit back together.
Knits broken bone. On a fracture that has not been set the bone knits crooked, so set it first.
Repairs burned skin and the tissue just under it.
Kills bacteria and fungi: treats wound infections, sepsis and other infections.
Binds and clears toxins from the blood before they reach the liver and kidneys.
Raises the oxygen the blood carries to the tissues, whatever the lungs are managing.
Repairs brain and nerve tissue. It cannot repair a brain that has died.
Repairs the eyes. It does not clear a clouded lens (cataracts need surgery).
Purges radiation from the body and limits the damage it does while it is purged.
Repairs damaged cells and DNA (genetic damage from radiation, cloning or mutagens).
Brings the core temperature back toward normal, from too hot or too cold.
Rebuilds lost blood volume: transfusions and the minerals the body makes blood from.
Supports the circulation: steadies the pulse and holds up the blood pressure.
Relieves pain. Pain relief also stops a patient flinching during surgery.
Raises the heart rate and breathing drive. It makes bleeding worse.
Repairs a synthetic's structural plating (welder, nanopaste).
Repairs a synthetic's wiring and burned circuits (cable coil, nanopaste).
Clears a synthetic's processor and system faults.
Recalibrates a synthetic's actuators and sensors (multitool).
Sews torn or perforated organ tissue shut during surgery.
Cuts away dead (necrotic) tissue and growths during surgery.
Clears and secures a blocked airway (an airway kit, the Heimlich manoeuvre).
Lets trapped air out of the chest so the lung can expand again (decompression needle, surgical decompression).
Shocks a heart in a shockable rhythm back into a normal one (defibrillator).
Chest compressions (CPR): keep some blood moving while the heart is stopped.
Adrenaline-type drugs: raise a collapsed blood pressure, shrink airway swelling and help restart a stopped heart.
Repairs the stomach, the bowel and the appendix.
Rehydrates: water, salts and sugar by mouth or drip. Also feeds the body's fight against a cold.
Stops a seizure and makes the next less likely.
Knocks opioids off their receptors: reverses an opioid overdose.
Packs or presses a bleeding wound shut (hemostatic gauze, pressure bandage).
Seals an open chest wound airtight (chest seal).
The body's own healing: works best on a fed, watered, resting and sleeping patient.
Full restoration (powers, magic, admin intervention): repairs every condition that can be repaired.
Feeds a nanoform's refactory with steel so it can rebuild itself.
Closes an organic incision at the end of surgery (cautery, sutures).
Closes and secures a synthetic's maintenance panel (screwdriver).
Sets a broken bone and closes a sawn bone layer (bone gel, bone setter).
Repairs a torn blood vessel or a cut artery during surgery (FixOVein).
Rejoins a severed tendon during surgery.
Takes out shrapnel, bullets and other embedded objects during surgery.
Breaks up deposits in the tissue with focused ultrasound during surgery.
Treats deep burns (charred and carbonised tissue) and burns of the airway, which ordinary burn care barely reaches.
Shrinks swelling in the airway, such as after breathing in fire.

article.title: Station Wiki
article.summary: Start here: what the wiki holds and how to find your way around it.

blocks.t: The station wiki holds the reference every department works from. Pick a section on the left, or search for anything by name.

items: Every underlined name is a link: follow it, and use the back and forward buttons to return.
Sections fold open and shut. The section of the page you are reading opens by itself.
Search matches titles, sections and summaries.
[[dept/command|Command]]: the heads of staff, communications and paperwork.
[[dept/security|Security]]: the officers, their weapons, armour and restraints.
[[dept/engineering|Engineering]]: power, atmospherics, construction, tools and the engines.
[[dept/medical|Medical]] and the [[med/index|medical reference]]: conditions, drugs, treatment mechanisms, symptoms, triggers, organs and surgery.
[[dept/research|Research]]: research nodes, robotics, exosuits, machine parts and [[chem/purity|chemistry]].
[[dept/civilian|Civilian]]: service, botany, the kitchen and the bar.
[[guide/chemistry/lab|Working the chemistry lab]] and [[guide/research/basics|research and fabrication]].
[[lore/index|The Traveler's Guide]]: the places, peoples, companies and governments of human space.
Anything not yet filed under a department is under Uncategorised, at the bottom of the index.

blocks.t: The medical and chemistry pages are generated from the game's own data, so they always match what happens on the station.
